paragraphs: Chapter 684
Episode 174. Beil's Delusion (4)
Inside the cabin of the ship Ram.
[Why did you save me when death doesn't truly come for me?]
Though his voice sounded calm, there was anger in Padler's words.

Originally, his neck should have been snapped by Beil's hand just now. Even though that doesn't mean death per se, the fact that he was forced to retreat from an enemy he deeply resented made him feel uncomfortable.
If he had fought like a vengeful spirit again, as he did during the first full-scale attack on the Sword Garden, he would have been able to continue the fight for a while, even without his neck.
[Reconstructing your physical and spiritual form takes some effort for me. I didn't want to waste it on something meaningless.]
Rosa responded calmly, but her words were laced with contempt and ridicule. Disdain for the weak, ridicule for the useless.
She saw most of the figures now occupying the Sword Garden in this way.
Once their metamorphosis into fiends was complete, she wouldn't even find a few of them who seemed slightly useful necessary anymore.
'This must have been how Siron saw us in the past.'
Just objects that made the ground she stood on a little less desolate and empty, ones she could easily wipe out with a single push or a breath.

Most members of her clan seemed like that to the current Rosa. Padler was one of the slightly better objects, but he was no different from other objects in that he always failed the tasks entrusted to him.
Those like Padler who remained in the spirit realm were no different.
Rosa realized that she was becoming a being who needed no one's help, but she felt no particular excitement.
The only thing that excited her was the youngest, Jin. Only when she thought of Jin or saw Jin did she wear a real smile, not a sneer.
Just like a few minutes ago when she summoned Padler, she saw Jin through his eyes and smiled.
[I hope this doesn't happen again.]
[Ah... is that so?]
Rosa contemplated whether to suppress Padler, then chuckled.
He often irritated Rosa because he did not submit to fear or power.

[It seems your resentment towards Runcandel is not as deep as I thought. All the avengers I've seen so far have always tried to survive in any situation to strike at their enemy... they didn't just flare up as if they were okay with ending up in any way, like you.]
[I'm not your slave, Rosa Runcandel. I'll decide that for myself.]
[That's right, you're not my slave. You're just a leftover from the past that exists in this world because of me. You're too useless to be my slave.]
Padler didn't react to Rosa's insulting words. Instead, he seemed to smirk as if he found it amusing.
[You spoke well. In fact, I don't need the help of a leftover like you, why don't you let me vanish?]
[For the same reason as you.]
Padler laughed again.
[Did you think you needed it, but you didn't?]
Rosa, locking eyes with him.
[Yes. Just as your revenge turned out to be virtually over, I didn't realize that my power would stabilize this quickly.]
Padler's revenge was indeed over.

[What I want is not the resurgence of Runcandel, but its corruption and destruction. The descendants of Temar, your mother. The power you, Rosa Runcandel, have chosen will ultimately lead Runcandel into the abyss.]
As he had said when he first fought with Jin, Padler wanted nothing but the destruction of Runcandel.
From the moment he first appeared in this world, he had nothing but blind hatred for Runcandel.
Therefore, Ilina didn't even need to take special measures to shatter his spirit or brainwash him. Instead, Ilina at the time planned to keep Rosa in check through Padler.
However, the moment he saw Rosa, who had become a fiend after that battle, Padler realized that his goal had already been achieved.
After all, the Sword Garden had become a land that could no longer be called Runcandel, and ultimately, she would bring about her own destruction and devour the entire world.
Ilina's plan to keep Rosa in check through Padler also lost its meaning. Even if there were a few more powerful beings like Padler, it would be impossible to keep her in check from within Runcandel.
Also, there was no need to keep her in check anymore. The fiend she had become was naturally dyeing the entire world with despair.
[Then why not just reclaim the power and destroy me? I don't understand why you're going through all this trouble.]
Just as Rosa was about to answer, Ilina spoke first.
"Lord Padler, it seems you are quite tired. You haven't been back in the world long, but you're already full of the desire to end your pitiful existence."
[Ilina.]
"But Lord Padler, the head of the household is now a god, not a human. Whether you exist is entirely in the hands of the head, and from what I know... most gods tend to respect the fate of mortals."
[Fate, what are you talking about all of a sudden?]
"Only those who have fulfilled their destiny can rest in obliteration. If your revenge was truly over, the head would have destroyed you in an instant, even if you didn't want it
. But that's not the case. You still have things left to do."
Padler glared at Ilina.

"How ridiculous is it that someone who used to be revered as one of the Ten Knights, has to rely on someone else's help to finish all his revenge? Shouldn't there be at least a little bit of it, something you have done yourself, for you to have the right to rest? By the way, the person you hate so much has just awakened......"
[Are you talking about Veil?]
"Yes, Veil Runcandel. You should eliminate him yourself, who is presumed to be another remnant of a god. By doing so, the High Lord will give you rest for having struggled to fulfill your destiny."
Padler was silent for a while, then turned to go outside.

[...Anyway, Veil will be no different from me the moment he stands in front of Lady Rosa. Lord, I can't understand why you, who are already prepared to end the world alone, are doing such a useless thing.]
"You don't need to understand the Lord's will."
[But I am a leftover, so I will join your game one more time.]
When he left the cabin, Ilina bowed her head to Rosa.
"I apologize if I overstepped, my Lord. He's insolent to the end. Those who have nothing to lose, no special desires, are the problem. But it's better than being incompetent and greedy."
[As Lord Padler said. I was considering obliterating you when you stood in my way.]
"I did it because it would be a waste."
[From your point of view, it could be. Your actions were presumptuous, but since your intention wasn't to belittle me as before, I'll let it go.]
"Thank you for understanding."

[I do not respect the destiny of humans, let alone Lords. The youngest one deserves respect. But if by today's events, Lord, you help with the story between me and the youngest, I'll reward you then. My thoughts might change a little.]
Ilina's expression brightened.
"I assure you it will be. Even after my mother wakes up, I will remain your most loyal servant......"
[Bring the second-generation riders tomorrow. Let them know that I will be punishing them for their past failure.]
"Understood."
Meanwhile, the Barmul alliance was looking up at the sky where the battle had ended underwater.
Whether it was because Padler had suddenly disappeared, Veil spread his golden aura all over the sky, revealing his anger.
Rosa only called Padler back as Ram.
[These lowly creatures, tell me where Padler ran away!]
The remaining Chaos Dragon, Black Line, knights, and Lionel and Star, all had to endure Veil's rage.
[Or run away too, I'll smash your hometown to pieces. Where is it, the castle of Runcandel?]
Lionel and Star were already in no condition to answer. Their bodies had been torn apart by Veil's energy because they had given way too much in trying to save Padler.
"What's the reason Rosa saved only Lord Padler? It doesn't seem like it's because she lacks the power to recall everyone else."
When Rosa looked down at the seabed through Padler's eyes, Jin felt a surge of Rosa's power from him.
It was an infinite power worthy of being called a god, pressing down on him momentarily.
'...Does she think there's no need to save the rest?'
As he thought that to Rosa, those who were less significant than Padler were practically of no help at all, he felt chills all over his body.
Rosa was getting stronger faster than him.
If she could transport herself outside of Huphester directly, he was certain that she could destroy the world within a few days.
A massive wall that seemed impossible to break was waiting for him beyond this sea.
"Jin?"
Valeria grabbed Jin's shoulder. Looking back, all his colleagues were looking at him with worried faces. Ever since Padler disappeared, Jin had unknowingly been wearing a worried expression.
Jin glanced at his colleagues and shook his head.
"Rosa has become stronger. I don't even understand why she had to save Padler now."
His colleagues nodded as if they understood.
"…Maybe the day when we will fight a decisive battle with Rosa could come sooner than we expected."
At that moment, he had a premonition that Rosa might be able to handle everyone alone without even caring about characters like Padler.
And unlike that monster, he would not fight alone.
"But it's not the time to worry about that now. It would be best to calm down the old Knight of the Ten first."
"Oh, Jin. Should I tell that guy to stop now?"
Jin nodded to Sandra and smiled.
"He'll stop on his own. All those who wanted to harm you are dead. But we need to help him face the truth."
Swoosh!
Jin drew his sword again.
"So you tell Lord Veil to deal with me. Warn him that the moment any of my colleagues get hurt, he will never see me again."
"What if something goes wrong with you!?"
"If I fight with the certainty that Lord Veil will never attack my colleagues, that will never happen."
